scope: SLP Chapter 2 (An Overview): sufficiency and uniqueness of the Euler and boundary conditions for the finite-horizon concave planning problem; the log/Cobb-Douglas finite-horizon solution (Ex 2.2) and infinite-horizon value function and Bellman equation (Ex 2.3); the neoclassical technology and the properties of f (Ex 2.1) with Cobb-Douglas as a model of the assumptions; the constant-savings-rate dynamics (Ex 2.4); the event-tree planner's dimension count and the sufficiency of the stochastic Euler equations (Ex 2.5); the stochastic Bellman equation and expected lifetime utility under i.i.d. shocks (Ex 2.6); Gaussian log capital with its means, variances and limits (Ex 2.7); competitive equilibrium, the first and second welfare theorems, firm-owned capital and sequential markets (Ex 2.8-2.10).
source: Stokey, Lucas and Prescott (1989), Recursive Methods in Economic Dynamics, Chapter 2.
